identity_notes: Pomegranate has a large legitimate human evidence base (81 kept of 156 screened) spanning cardiometabolic, exercise, renal, rheumatologic, cognitive, and reproductive-health indications. The retrieved abstracts for many primary trials and meta-analyses were truncated in this scope before the results/conclusion sentence, so a large share of kept records have primary_result_quote set to null with direction_primary 'unresolved' -- this reflects a genuine gap in the retrieved data, not lack of screening effort, and the curator should re-pull full abstracts for any shortlisted item before drawing conclusions. Several endpoints (lipid profile, blood pressure, oxidative stress) each have 3-4 overlapping meta-analyses published over time (e.g., lipid profile: 26857863 2016, 31987256 2019, 40216355 2025, 42153011 2026; blood pressure: 27888156 2017, 37461211 2023, 38410857 2024); the most recent/largest of each cluster should generally be weighted over earlier ones. A material form distinction recurs throughout: juice, whole fruit/extract, seed oil, and peel extract/powder are chemically different preparations (seed oil is fatty-acid/phytoestrogen-dominant vs. juice/peel being polyphenol/ellagitannin-dominant) and several kept records are flagged related_form_differs accordingly (28323626 seed oil; 35229548/39608758 peel extract; 37529273/39055198 peel powder in a bread/chapatti food matrix). Multiple food-drug CYP3A4-interaction studies test pomegranate juice against grapefruit juice as an active comparator (25720525, 27294349) and a broader interaction review (29703387) covers many juices, not pomegranate alone -- all flagged for interaction handoff. A dedicated adverse-effects systematic review exists (37116077) and should be the primary safety reference; a pediatric case report of dietary-pattern-related transient hyperphosphatasemia (34094744) also names pomegranate juice in its title though the retrieved abstract text itself is generic. No record in this scope reported a retraction or expression of concern specific to a pomegranate clinical study (the one retracted record found, 35436290, is an unrelated agronomy/soil-nutrient study).
